note: [agent-bulk] shw 25015 (155.0 MeV, 10 seg, 47.1 cm, gamma1 of reco pi0 group 0) - I looked and could not separate two readings, so this is unclear and here they are. What the pictures show (shw25015-az-055-el+20 and -az+085-el+20, frame half-span 60 cm): a compact core of 4-5 members in the first ~25 cm from the X, then FOUR detached fragments strung out along the same axis at 46.6, 50.6, 75.7 and 99-100 cm with large empty gaps between them - 110033 (0.34 cm, 3.0 deg), 112035 (7.61 cm, 12.6 deg), 106027 (2.11 cm, 2.1 deg), 109031+109032 (2.23+6.80 cm, 10-11 deg), all absorbed by pass4_angle, the last two beyond the 80 cm tier-1 line. Reading (a) OVER-CLUSTERED: a 155 MeV EM cascade is essentially over by 5-6 radiation lengths (70-85 cm in LAr) and cannot plausibly be 100 cm long; those far stubs are separate objects and including them inflates E1 and hence the stored pi0 mass. The event also contains a 188.3 cm muon (18009, unowned) running roughly PARALLEL to this shower at 15-30 cm separation, so fragments 'along the shower axis' at 50-100 cm are equally well described as muon-associated deltas - 112035 is only 5.3 cm from that muon. Reading (b) CORRECT: the acceptance plot has NO non-member circle anywhere in range, so nothing is missing; the member set is one direction and one apex (all members 0-16 deg, monotone in distance, no second apex on either azimuth); and doc pr/116 section 2.3 records exactly this shape - a chain of stubs strung along the axis out to 88 cm - being called correct on evt284791 with the explicit caveat that far-stub membership was untested. I cannot break the tie from the display. CORRECTION I made on myself: I first read 106027 as sitting ON the muon in both azimuths and was going to mark it OUT; computing the 3-D min distance from state.json gives 16.9 cm, so that was a projection coincidence and the mark is withdrawn. No segment marks recorded - I have no piece I can name with confidence, which is the same reason pr/116 section 2.2 left evt280159 unmarked. Also examined: shw 105026 (65.0 MeV, 1 seg, 11.1 cm, gamma2), a short zigzag with a diffuse cloud ~30 cm off the vertex and 13 cm off the muon; single apex, and the only thing it might be missing is 104025 (2.31 cm at 14.4 cm / 25.9 deg, tier 1) which at 26 deg is too marginal for me to call. PI0: the reco pairing 25015+105026 looks topologically sound on pio-az-055-el+020 - both gamma starts are detached from the magenta vertex star and both axes point away from it. But the mass is entirely convention-dependent here and the reco took the largest angle: stored 150.6 MeV (theta 97.2 deg, inside the accept window), display axis convention 108.6 MeV (theta 65.5 deg), display vertex convention 56.4 MeV (theta 32.6 deg). The two gamma arrows in the picture look far closer to 40 deg than to 97 deg, but I will not claim an angle off a projection. This is the pr/114 section 6.1 inconsistency, not a new finding, but it is worth knowing that this event's accepted pi0 depends on it. Scope: 2 showers of 13 examined; 11 skipped by the <20 MeV rule and not looked at. The vtx-* sweep is half-span 213 cm (the 188 cm muon) so it was used for topology only; the vertex itself looks fine - the star sits where the muon and a second grey track meet.
